connection: Earlier ScratchPad sessions remain unchanged. Create a dedicated Session05 folder containing one small class per exercise, then use Program.cs only as the application's entry point for constructing and running each exercise.
objectives: Identify a method signature, arguments, parameters, and return value.
Trace values into and out of a method call.
Place each method exercise in a session-specific class and invoke it from the application's entry point.

visuals.title: Arguments enter a method
visuals.explanation: A call supplies argument values to parameters; control enters the method and later returns to the caller.

visuals.title: Parameters and locals stay scoped
visuals.explanation: Parameters and local variables are available inside their method boundary, preventing unrelated code from depending on temporary details.

visuals.title: Return sends one result back
visuals.explanation: A return value crosses the method boundary and lets the caller decide what to do with the result.

visuals.title: The signature is a contract
visuals.explanation: Return type, method name, and parameter list describe how callers may use the method.

preQuiz.prompt: What is scheduledHours in CalculateVariance(recordedHours, scheduledHours)?
options: An argument at the call site
preQuiz.explanation: The call supplies the current value as an argument; the method receives it through a parameter.

preQuiz.prompt: Can a local variable declared inside CalculateVariance be read directly in top-level code?
options: No, its scope is the method body
preQuiz.explanation: A local is only in scope within its declaring block.

preQuiz.prompt: Why return a decimal from CalculateVariance?
options: So the caller receives the calculated value
preQuiz.explanation: The method produces a decimal result that the caller can store or use.

concept.title: A method names a unit of behavior
paragraphs: A method groups statements behind a name. A good name lets the caller express intent while the body owns calculation details.

Session 05 uses fresh examples instead of rewriting earlier-session code. Each example lives in its own class file so the exercise has a clear boundary. Classes are taught properly in Session 06; for now, use the provided class wrapper and focus on the methods inside it.

concept.title: Parameters receive values
paragraphs: Arguments are expressions at the call site. Parameters are local names in the method declaration. By default, C# passes the resulting values by value.
In this session, method examples use decimal and string values. Reference-type behavior is a separate topic taught in a later session.
concept.code: static decimal CalculateVariance(decimal recordedHours, decimal scheduledHours)

concept.title: Scope limits dependencies
paragraphs: A local variable exists only inside the method body that declares it. A parameter is also local to its method, even when an argument at the call site has a similar name.
return ends the method and supplies its result to the caller.
concept.code:
decimal difference = recordedHours - scheduledHours;
return difference;

lab.objective: Practice method declarations, parameters, local scope, and return values in seven isolated Session 05 classes.

Every referenced application artifact was created in this session or an earlier session.
Earlier production code, tests, and ScratchPad session files remain unchanged.

postQuiz.prompt: Where is difference available in Session05Lab05?
postQuiz.explanation: It is a local declared inside CalculateVariance, so code outside that method cannot use it directly.

postQuiz.prompt: What changes if CalculateVariance returns scheduledHours - recordedHours?
options: The sign and meaning of variance
postQuiz.explanation: Reversing operands preserves compilation but changes semantics.

postQuiz.prompt: Why can ClassifyVariance be tested through application output here?
postQuiz.explanation: The caller displays the returned status, making the result observable.

reflections: Which details are hidden behind each named method call?
When would a method with many parameters signal a design problem?
How does return type constrain callers?
whatBreaks: Removing a Session 05 class while Program.cs still constructs it prevents the ScratchPad from compiling. Removing CalculateVariance leaves its Run method without the numeric result. Removing a return statement prevents a non-void method from compiling, while trying to read difference outside Session05Lab05.CalculateVariance fails because that local name is out of scope.
summary: Methods name behavior. Arguments produce values for parameters, locals stay within scope, and return values carry results back to callers.
